overall_summary: Deduplication and recent performance analysis reveal that space-based 'What If' scenarios and extreme planetary facts (specifically involving extreme conditions like diamond planets and unique cosmic objects) generate the highest views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes/views and comments/views). Older or less interactive topics such as psychological tricks and simple animal facts show significantly lower velocity.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Space Survival ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) lead in views and likes-per-view compared to standard static facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical immersive space scenarios involving extreme planetary environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing surreal phenomena such as 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (v1rrcZLdp4U) capture immediate attention and high organic traction.
winning_patterns.action: Focus future scripts on rare, counterintuitive physical properties of celestial bodies.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on memory creation and songs stuck in your head (e.g., ef3ND4qiRHc, 5AN7LUgqarc) maintain very low views and near-zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological trivia in favor of high-performing space and physics content.

weak_patterns.evidence: Simple animal anatomy facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (AXAfwrzzEdU) yield lower relative velocity compared to high-concept space themes.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal-related content toward cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary anomalies rather than basic trivia.
